messages:
elaine: Pushed two quick comps for the streaming handoff + prompt library insert — need UX + a11y take. GIFs in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/stream-handoff (see frames 3 & 4). Option 1 = mini floating toolbar anchored to the latest message (Stop / Retry / Insert prompt). Option 2 = persistent bottom rail with token counter + controls. Which feels less noisy when the stream is active? marc: Saw both. Leaning mini toolbar — feels more contextual and keeps the conversation flow cleaner. Also easier to show a tiny token badge near the message instead of a giant meter. sanjay: mini toolbar okay, but accessibility concerns: floating controls must be keyboard-focusable and reachable by screen readers. If it's anchored to each message we need a deterministic focus order. Also how do we announce live tokens to SR users? ari: +1 to keyboard focus concerns. For streaming text, we should expose an `aria-live="polite"` region for incremental content and a separate hidden region for final completion announcement (e.g., "generation complete, controls available"). That lets screen readers know when actions appear. olivia: Copy nits: "Stop" vs "Pause" vs "Cancel" — I think primary action should read "Stop" (clear intent). For Retry, choose "Regenerate" not "Retry" to match product language. Token counter label should be "Tokens used" not just a number tooltip. elaine: Good call on copy. Also thinking about a micro affordance for prompt library insert: a tiny + icon that opens a compact modal; avoids jarring the conversation. In mini toolbar it would be a single icon; in bottom rail it can be a text button. marc: One downside of bottom rail is it competes with other console footers (logs, prompt library, files). But it is more discoverable for new users. Maybe we show bottom rail only for first-time sessions, then switch to mini toolbar after a preference cookie? sanjay: If we go that route, ensure keyboard shortcut to toggle controls (e.g., `Ctrl+.`) and announce that in the help menu. Also make sure the token counter isn't read every update — that's noisy. It should only announce on threshold changes or on completion. ari: Quick snippet for announcing completion for screen readers — maybe: ```html
...chunks...
// when done: document.getElementById('announce-complete').textContent = 'Response complete. Controls available.'; ``` olivia: a11y contrast: the mini toolbar icons currently use 50% gray on hover — fails WCAG for small icon targets. Need 3:1 contrast at minimum for icon-only interactive elements. Also add visible focus ring matching system focus color. elaine: noted. I can update the comps: increase icon contrast, add 44px hit target with inner 24px icon, and show focus state as 2px outline. marc: Performance note: streaming handoff must not re-render the whole thread on each token. Use a mutable DOM append strategy + virtualization. Also keep token counter updates debounced (250-500ms) to avoid jank. ux-bot: Design checklist reminder: ensure (1) keyboard nav for toolbar, (2) aria-live for streaming region, (3) announce completion, (4) token counter with optional hide for SR, (5) focus management after regenerate. sanjay: One more edge: mobile. Floating toolbar might obscure reply composers on small viewports. On mobile prefer an inline compact control row above composer. Figma has a mobile frame? elaine: I added a mobile frame in the file. Mobile will default to compact inline row. Thanks for the feedback — I'll iterate and post updated GIFs tomorrow. If anyone has strong objections to mini toolbar vs bottom rail call it out now, otherwise I'll push the mini toolbar as default and add an experimental bottom rail for newbies. :thumbsup:
